documentationFeedback: codegraph.go's WarmCodegraphIndex doc and docs/kubernetes.md say the index a stop leaves partial 'is repaired by the next warm-up' / 'which codegraph index repairs'. Measured: true for a build stopped 12 s in (run B, 55 s), but a build stopped 5 s in left a database CodeGraph's own `codegraph index` wedged on — its watchdog killed it after 60 s ('Main thread unresponsive for ~60s … #850'), leaving a 155 KB database with fileCount 0 and index.state 'indexing' — and only the launch after that rebuilt it (run F3, 42 s). The warm-up's lease handling is right throughout; the sentence should say the repair can take a second launch, since CodeGraph 1.5.0 does not always recover its own interrupted build in one `index`.

implementerProof.how: Round 2 (head e865b2c1, fix 29bdf099): drove the implementer's stop-mid-build scenario independently with the branch's `legion worker-shim --pod-safety --warm-codegraph` (built here from e865b2c1 with Go 1.26.8 fetched into the pod) wrapping the real Oh My Pi against a fake daemon that acks the hello, on fresh clones at e865b2c1 — a SIGTERM to the whole process group 12 s and 5 s into the build, and to the shim alone 12 s in: every time the shim was gone within 0.12–0.30 s of the signal, `.codegraph/legion-warm.lock` was released, no codegraph process remained, the warm-up logged its end, and the stopped codegraph child was reaped (no zombie), so the relaunch's CodeGraph did not see a live lock holder. The relaunch on the 12 s kill repaired the partial index to complete in 55 s. Negative control: the identical group-SIGTERM drive with the pre-fix `legion` built from 386f5a37 left the lease behind with no log line, as round 1 found. My red test TestWorkerShimLetsAnInFlightWarmUpReleaseItsLeaseBeforeItExits, untouched by the fix, passes 3/3 at e865b2c1; it failed 3/3 at 386f5a37. Rows 1a–1d, 1e (both ways), 2a and 3a–3c re-driven at this head with the same results as round 1; the implementer's recorded figures held, and the round-2 proof's run B/C/D/E observations match mine.

observations: Round 1's failure is fixed on the real surface: on a group SIGTERM, a shim-only SIGTERM and a normal completion the shim exits only once the warm-up has returned, 0.12–0.30 s after the signal (bounds: codegraphStopGrace 5 s, warmUpDrain 10 s, the launcher's StopGrace 30 s), with the agent's status 143 and the lease released.

A second effect of the fix: the stopped codegraph child is reaped by the shim (cmd.Run's Wait) instead of being orphaned to PID 1. In a pre-#1752 pod PID 1 is the shim and reaps nothing, so the pre-fix binary's child lingered as a zombie, and CodeGraph's FileLock (utils.js: a lock under 2 minutes old whose PID answers kill(pid, 0) is live) refused the relaunch's `codegraph index` with exit 1 — the message goes to stdout, so the warm-up's log line showed an empty error. Under #1752 the launcher is PID 1 and reaps orphans, so this would not have shown there; it does not arise with the fixed shim.

CodeGraph's `codegraph status --json` reports index.state complete up to about a second before `codegraph init` exits (run D: status complete at 52.7 s with the init process and the lease still present; the lease was released once init returned). A poll that reads 'complete' is therefore at most a second ahead of the lease's release.

Which `[legion]` line the stop logs depends on a race the fix tolerates: when the codegraph child dies on the group signal before the shim's loop ends, `codegraph init failed for … (exit -1)` (run A); when the loop ends first, `… ended with its process before codegraph init finished` (runs A2, C, F1). Both release the lease.

A stop 5 s into a build (runs A2, F1) can leave a database CodeGraph's next `codegraph index` wedges on (watchdog kill at 60 s, database reset to its schema, state 'indexing'); the following launch's warm-up then rebuilds it to complete (run F3: 42 s). A bare `codegraph init` killed with SIGTERM at 5 s by `timeout` (run G) was repaired by one `codegraph index` in 33 s, so the wedge depends on where the kill lands. The warm-up converges across launches because each role's launch runs it once; a single role relaunched once may sit 60 s on the wedge with nothing running until another role starts. Recorded as documentationFeedback, not a failure: the lease and relaunch behaviour this round fixes hold, and the per-launch build time (acceptance 2's figure) is 32–73 s on a fresh workspace.
